Out in the Open: An NSA-Proof Twitter, Built With Code From Bitcoin and BitTorrent

Maybe it's because I'm old but I just don't "get" Twitter. It's utterly stupid and completely useless...unless used for purposes of an emergency. There's nothing that it does that other social media platforms can do far better.

In any case, I bring this up to promote the best secure messaging app that I've ever used: SIMSme. It's written by DeutschePost and the servers are located in Germany. They do NOT comply with USDOJ information requests. All messages are end-to-end encrypted with AES256 and the app recognizes if there's a MitM attack happening--so it's "Stingray-proof." It's as easy to use as text messaging...plus you see when your recipient reads your messages, you can send voice messages and attachments, you can send group messages, and (best of all) you can set a time (say 10 seconds)--or a date and time-- when the messages will self-destruct. The source code is freely available for anyone to see and to vet. I have tested the code using a "Stingray" of my own design (basically an IMSI catcher that works IRT) and all you get if the signal is intercepted is random garbage. NOTHING is stored on your phone if you don't want it to be. Your security is exactly as good as your passphrase is complex.

This app has revolutionized how I communicate and, of course, it's free. I cannot recommend it highly enough--it's now my most-used application. It's available for Android...not sure about other platforms though.

American Securities and Exchange Commission says Israeli citizens, sold short a list of 38 stocks that could reasonably be expected to fall in value as a result of the pending attacks.

These speculators operated out of the Toronto, Canada and Frankfurt, Germany, stock exchanges and their profits were specifically stated to be in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Christopher Bollyn.

Prison Planet Mystery Speculator Bets On Disaster, Pat Shannan, American Free Press, Monday Sept 3, 2007

The 9-11 attacks were foreshadowed by “put” options placed onAmerican and UnitedAirlines, as reported in the immediate aftermath. According to CBS News, the put ratio for United Airlines was 25 times above normal on September 6.

In the week before September 11, “put” options in United and American Airlines went through a furious and unprecedented spasm of investment. Most of the investments in these put options originated in Germany through the Deutsche Bank.

Deutsche Bank had earlier acquired Banker’s Trust, an investment banking firm whose vice chairman in charge of “private client relations” in the late 1990s was A. B. “Buzzy” Krongard.

In March of 2001, Krongard was appointed executive director of the CIA. On September 6-7, when there was no significant news or stock price movement involving United, the Chicago exchange handled 4,744 “put” options for UAL stock, compared with just 396 call options.

Essentially bets that the price will rise.When the market re-opened on Sept. 17, 2001, American and United, the only two airlines with hijacked planes, saw their stocks plummet by around 40%.

What becomes particularly relevant in the lead-up to 9-11 is the August CIA briefing of President Bush concerning the potential threat of attacks by bin Laden using hijacked planes on certain sites, such as the Pentagon and World Trade Center, and the fact that the CIA had bugging equipment on bin Laden messages and international banking operations.

“Put” options on Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, two of the World Trade Center’s most prominent occupants, also spiked in the days before 9-11. The 9-11 Investigation Committee made no attempt to pursue this highly sensitive matter. The SEC never made public who these speculators were.

Minesweeper has always been a fun game for me because of the focus on logical thinking, and the satisfying progression of clearing a board. One of my biggest frustrations with the game, however, is how you can get forced into situations where you must guess, i.e:

111_
1X21
12AB
_1CD

Where if you have two mines left, they could be at either A and D or B and C.

I recently found a open-source version of minesweeper which guarantees that every puzzle is solvable. It is quite fun to play as you no longer give up on an opening or end-game because it appears unsolvable. If you enjoy the game, I'd recommend trying it out. The author also has a bunch of other puzzles on his site.
